facts.statement: Atsinganosaurus was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in what is now France during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Atsinganosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which existed in what is now France during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The only known remains of Atsinganosaurus were collected from the Grès à Reptiles Formation of the Aix-en-Provence Basin.
facts.quote: Well-preserved remains (and the only known) of Atsinganosaurus were collected from the Grès à Reptiles Formation of the Aix-en-Provence Basin.

facts.statement: Atsinganosaurus was first described by Géraldine Garcia, Sauveur Amico, Francois Fournier, Eudes Thouand, and Xavier Valentin in 2010.
facts.quote: Atsinganosaurus was first described by Géraldine Garcia, Sauveur Amico, Francois Fournier, Eudes Thouand and Xavier Valentin in 2010

facts.statement: Excavations at the Velaux-La Bastide Neuve site were carried out between 2009 and 2010 by the Palaios Association and the University of Poitiers.
facts.quote: Between 2009 and 2010, excavations were carried out at the Grès à Reptiles Formation at Velaux-La Bastide Neuve by the Palaios Association and the University of Poitiers.

facts.statement: The holotype of Atsinganosaurus consists of four posterior dorsal vertebrae discovered alongside remains of another titanosaurian named Garrigatitan.
facts.quote: The holotype of Atsinganosaurus, VBN.93.01.a-d, a set of four posterior dorsal vertebrae, was discovered along with the remains of Garrigatitan, another titanosaurian.

facts.statement: The fossil site of La Bastide Neuve near Velaux in the Bouches-du-Rhône department was discovered in 1992 by Xavier Valentin.
facts.quote: El sitio de La Bastide Neuve está cerca de la ciudad de Velaux en el departamento francés de Bouches-du-Rhône y fue descubierto en 1992 por Xavier Valentin.

facts.statement: The well-preserved bones of Atsinganosaurus were found in an area of six square meters.
facts.quote: Los huesos están bien conservados y fueron descubiertos en un área de seis metros cuadrados.

facts.statement: Atsinganosaurus fossils were found alongside remains of turtles, crocodilian teeth, theropods, nodosaurids, and rhadinodontids.
facts.quote: Los huesos fueron encontrados junto con los restos de otros vertebrados como tortugas y los dientes de cocodrilomorfos, terópodos, nodosáuridos y rabdodóntidos.

facts.statement: The holotype material consists of four connected caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: El material holotipo, VBN.03.01.a, b, c, d se compone de cuatro vértebras caudales conectadas.

facts.statement: The generic name Atsinganosaurus derives from the Greek word for "gypsy," referring to a possible east-to-west migration of the species.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico deriva de la palabra griega "τσιγγάνος" o "αθίγγανος", que significa "gitano", que se refiere a la posible migración de este a oeste de la especie.

facts.statement: Atsinganosaurus lived approximately 75 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The time range for Atsinganosaurus is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2018 cladistic analysis places Atsinganosaurus in the lithostrotian clade Lirainosaurinae alongside Ampelosaurus and Lirainosaurus.
facts.quote: A 2018 cladistic analysis of Titanosauria places Ampelosaurus, Atsinganosaurus, and Lirainosaurus in the new lithostrotian clade Lirainosaurinae.

facts.statement: It is suggested that Atsinganosaurus is a basal representative of Lithostrotia based on a combination of primitive and derived titanosaurian features, though no published phylogenetic analysis confirms this.
facts.quote: Aunque no hay análisis filogenéticos publicados, se supone por esta combinación de características que Atsinganosaurus sea un representante basal de Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Later estimates suggest adults of Atsinganosaurus reached lengths of 5.38 to 8.95 meters and weighed between 2.46 and 5.26 metric tons.
facts.quote: Díez Díaz et al. (2021) reportedly corrected the estimates to 5.38-8.95 m and 2.46-5.26 MT.

facts.statement: Atsinganosaurus was a slender titanosaurian.
facts.quote: Atsinganosaurus era un titanosauriano delgado.

facts.statement: Atsinganosaurus possessed cylindrical tooth roots and spatulate tooth crowns.
facts.quote: Por ejemplo, la raíz cilíndrica y las coronas de los dientes tienen una forma espatulada.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Atsinganosaurus consists of five vertebrae with a concave posterior surface, a condition known as opisthocoelous.
facts.quote: El sacro consta de cinco vérterbras con la parte trasera cóncava, opistocélica.

facts.statement: The distal end of the humerus in Atsinganosaurus expands in a slightly oblique manner.
facts.quote: El extremo inferior del húmero se expande de forma levemente oblicua.

facts.statement: Atsinganosaurus is the fourth Late Cretaceous European titanosaurian discovered, following Lirainosaurus, Ampelosaurus, and Magyarosaurus.
facts.quote: Este género es, después de Lirainosaurus, Ampelosaurus y Magyarosaurus , el cuarto titanosauriano descubierto del Cretácico Superior de Europa.
